content.comment_body: I am trying to upload a [document] project to my [product_name], but I just get a vague error message box: [IMAGE] When I try 'Deploy to SD Card' it completes, but the SD Card contains only _dirmeta.dat and no project files. The SD Card is formatted to FAT32 and it's 4 GB. Diagnostics in Hardware > SD Card says 'Micro SD Card: OK'. [product_name] BM [article_no] Firmware: [version_no] [document] [version_no]
Which [product_name] model do you have exactly? Please provide the full article number.
Yes, that's the right one. It's a [product_name] [version_no] with two webservers. Could you upload your [document] project as a ZIP file?
It's just a test project, but I'm sending it anyway.

I have the latest [document] [version_no]. I can upgrade your project from [version_no] to [version_no] and then upload it without issues. I think the problem may be with the SD Card. Try using a different SD Card for testing.

I finally installed [document] [version_no] but still can't upload or write to the SD Card. Tried another SD Card: [product_name] couldn't read it. Tried a third SD Card: now [document] gives me this error message: [IMAGE] I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong, and I don't have any more SD Cards to test.

Turns out the issue was on my end. I thought 'UPLOAD' would send the project to the [product_name], but it actually uploads the project to the PC. This terminology is confusing. To get the project onto the [product_name], you need to hit 'DOWNLOAD'. It's not very intuitive, but thanks for the help.

[user_name] is correct—the terminology for upload and download in this interface is confusing. I've made the same mistake and spent hours troubleshooting, assuming the SD Card was at fault, before finding this post.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced confusion due to unclear 'Upload' and 'Download' functions in the [document] software, mistakenly believing technical issues or SD Card formatting were preventing project deployment to the [product_name] hardware. Significant troubleshooting efforts revealed that misleading interface terminology was the actual source of confusion, causing unnecessary workflow disruption.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to provide clear, intuitive options for transferring projects between PC and hardware, along with easily understood error messages. They want the deployment process to be straightforward and free from ambiguity in action selection.
